results.title: Odisha: CM Mohan Majhi, Union Minister Chouhan lead Anti-Anarchy march of BJP in Bhubaneswar
results.description: BHUBANESWAR: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on November 15 organised a massive ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ (Ganatantra Banchaao, Arajakata Hatao) march in Bhubaneswar, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and BJP national spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi participating in the campaign. The march, organised by the Bhubaneswar organisational district unit of the BJP, began from the party’s State headquarters and culminated at Vani Vihar. Several senior party leaders and workers joined the procession, which was aimed at highlighting the BJP’s concerns over what it described as attempts to undermine democratic institutions and create political instability in the country. ‘People have rejected Congress’s politics’: Shivraj Singh Chouhan Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who participated in the march, alleged that Rahul Gandhi, the Congress and the INDIA bloc were joining hands with anti-national elements to discredit the country’s armed forces, constitutional framework and institutions. माननीय मुख्यमंत्री श्री @MohanMOdisha जी के साथ आज भुवनेश्वर में 'लोकतंत्र बचाओ, अराजकता हटाओ' पदयात्रा में सहभागिता की। भुवनेश्वर की सड़कों पर उमड़ा जनसैलाब, जनता का उत्साह और लोकतंत्र के प्रति अटूट विश्वास अद्भुत है। जनता जागरूक है, लोकतंत्र मजबूत है और अराजकता फैलाने वालों… pic.twitter.com/fYcQHoQ9fS — Shivraj Singh Chouhan (@ChouhanShivraj) November 14, 2026 He termed such attempts condemnable and said the people of the country had completely rejected what he described as the Congress’s politics of anarchy and appeasement. ‘Congress is expressing frustration over prolonged loss of power’: Sudhanshu Trivedi BJP national spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi alleged that the Congress was adopting double standards on electronic voting machines (EVMs) and the Election Commission. He said the Congress accepted the credibility of EVMs and the Election Commission in states where it won elections but raised allegations of vote theft when the BJP emerged victorious. Read More: Arms Infiltration Alert: Myanmar national caught with sophisticated weapons and ammunition in Manipur; Two escape Referring to the Congress’s electoral setbacks in Odisha, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal, Trivedi said the party’s leaders were unable to come to terms with repeated electoral defeats and their declining political position. He alleged that the Congress was raising the slogan of ‘vote chori’ from Parliament to the streets to divert attention from its own failures. “Congress is expressing its frustration after remaining out of power for a prolonged period,” Trivedi said. ‘Protecting democracy is our commitment’: Majhi Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said India was progressing rapidly under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and had emerged as the world’s fourth-largest economy. He said the BJP-led double-engine government in Odisha had brought positive changes in the lives of the poor, farmers, women and youth. Referring to the Prime Minister’s vision of a developed India by 2047, Majhi said the country was witnessing economic growth alongside a reduction in poverty. However, he alleged that the Congress and certain opposition parties were attempting to create instability because they could not accept the country’s progress. ଅପପ୍ରଚାର ଓ ଅରାଜକତା ବିରୁଦ୍ଧରେ, ସମ୍ବିଧାନ ଏବଂ ଗଣତାନ୍ତ୍ରିକ ମୂଲ୍ୟବୋଧର ସୁରକ୍ଷା ପାଇଁ ଜନଜାଗରଣର ଉଦ୍‌ଘୋଷ – 'ଗଣତନ୍ତ୍ର ବଞ୍ଚାଅ, ଅରାଜକତା ହଟାଅ'। #SaveDemocracyRemoveAnarchy pic.twitter.com/mFg7Sju7W0 — Mohan Charan Majhi (@MohanMOdisha) November 14, 2026 The Chief Minister criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and alleged that he was acting at the behest of foreign divisive forces. He also termed the opposition’s allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls baseless, unreasonable and misleading. According to Majhi, opposition parties were questioning the Election Commission not in the interest of ordinary voters but to protect their alleged vote banks comprising deceased persons, people who had changed their addresses, illegal infiltrators and fake voters. He further alleged that opposition leaders, frustrated by their loss of political power, were raising the issue of instability and regime change. Such attempts to protect the interests of non-citizens at the cost of the country’s democratic framework would not be tolerated, he said. “Protecting democracy is our commitment,” Majhi asserted. BJP targets BJD over its ‘equidistance’ stand In his address, Chief Minister Majhi also criticised the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), alleging that its participation in supporting a Congress candidate in the Rajya Sabha election in Odisha, attending a Congress and I.N.D.I. Alliance meeting in Delhi and joining an I.N.D.I. Alliance rally had exposed the party’s claim of maintaining equal distance from both the BJP and Congress. He said these developments had revealed the BJD’s political position and called upon people to take the message of ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ to every household across the State. Majhi further said that with public support, the alleged conspiracies of forces attempting to create anarchy would be countered through democratic means. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute to building a prosperous Odisha. Senior BJP leaders participate The march witnessed the participation of several senior BJP leaders, including Bhubaneswar district president Niranjan Mishra, former State BJP president Sameer Mohanty, MLA Babu Singh, former minister Aravinda Dhali, former MLA Priyadarshi Mishra, State Executive Committee member Jagannath Pradhan and district in-charge and State secretary Saroj Kar. A large number of party leaders, office-bearers and workers from Bhubaneswar and other parts of the State also took part in the procession.
